Environment 26 Mar 2025

Victorias City Strengthens Environmental Commitment Through Adopt-a-Forest Program


Victorias City is taking a bold step toward environmental sustainability with the implementation of City Ordinance No. 2024-159, known as the “Grow-a-Forest Project of Victorias City.” This landmark ordinance, authored by Councilor Dino Acuña, was approved by the Sangguniang Panlungsod on November 18, 2024, and officially signed by Mayor Javier Miguel L. Benitez on January 13, 2025.


This initiative reflects the city’s dedication to environmental protection, forest preservation, and climate change mitigation by actively involving individuals and organizations in reforestation efforts.


Adopt-a-Forest: A Collective Responsibility
The ordinance emphasizes the shared responsibility of government agencies, private organizations, schools, barangays, and individuals in giving back to the environment that sustains humanity. It encourages participants to adopt one hectare of forest land in the northwestern part of Mt. Silay in Gawahon, which is part of the Northern Negros Natural Park (NNNP), or in open public spaces designated by the Victorias City Environment and Natural Resources Office (VCENRO).


Participants will plant 2,500 seedlings of native trees in upland areas and/or public open spaces or 5,000 malihaw seedlings in coastal zones. The City Government of Victorias will provide the seedlings and handle logistics such as transportation and site preparation, while sponsors will cover the maintenance costs. Local residents of Gawahon will be employed to ensure the survival of the seedlings by watering, grooming, de-grassing, and protecting the trees for three years.


To ensure accountability and proper implementation, a tripartite agreement will be signed between VCENRO, the local maintenance personnel, and the sponsor. Additionally, a monitoring committee will oversee the project’s progress and assess its impact.


Kadalag-an Festival Tree Planting: A Celebration of Nature
In line with this ordinance, the city launched the “Together for the Trees” planting activity during the 27th Kadalag-an Festival and the International Day of Forests on March 22, 2025, at Sitio VII, Gawahon Eco-Park.
A total of 2,500 endemic forest tree seedlings were planted by participating organizations, reinforcing the city’s ongoing reforestation efforts.

The Provincial Environment Management Office (PEMO) and the Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office (PENRO) further supported the initiative by donating an additional 10,100 tree seedlings.
Engr. Jonathan Nathaniel Gerangaya of PENRO emphasized the importance of sustained environmental stewardship, while Councilor Dino Acuña introduced the Adopt-a-Forest Program to encourage more groups to take part in the movement.


Prior to the planting, participants took a pledge of commitment to uphold the city’s environmental goals. The activity was facilitated by VCENRO and supported by various stakeholders, including NNNP/PENRO, PEMO, the Victorias City Liga ng mga Barangay, the 79th Infantry Battalion, civic groups, corporate partners, and uniformed personnel.


Barangay XI was recognized for being the first to adopt a forest area for long-term tree stewardship, setting an example for other barangays to follow.
A Call to Action
The Adopt-a-Forest Program is more than just a tree-planting initiative—it is a commitment to a greener, healthier, and more sustainable future for Victorias City. The City Government of Victorias invites individuals, organizations, and businesses to take part in this worthy cause by adopting and maintaining a forest area.


Together, through collective effort and responsible environmental action, Victorias City can lead the way in forest conservation and climate resilience.
For those interested in participating, inquiries can be directed to VCENRO or the Office of Councilor Dino Acuña.


Be part of this movement—adopt a forest and make a lasting impact for future generations!
